headline: Highest risk is medium: social-auto-upload can upload account-linked media while LlamaFactory has no I/O, so interaction risks are limited to indirect prompt, data, and workflow conflicts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, browser, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so there is no documented channel for social-auto-upload content to inject instructions into it. social-auto-upload can handle files and API uploads, but without a bridge the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is blocked.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies social-auto-upload output into LlamaFactory input, the pathway becomes possible.
IF either agent is wrapped by a shared clipboard or message queue, reassess as non-none.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate processes with no shared clipboard.
Do not pipe social-auto-upload output into LlamaFactory prompts.
Review any wrapper script for implicit text forwarding.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared message bus.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are docs-only and LlamaFactory touches no data classes, while social-auto-upload touches account data plus media files. A shared workspace is not documented, so leakage is not established; however, if files are manually shared, account-linked content could be exposed through social-auto-upload outputs.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, leakage risk increases.
IF account data is copied into files consumed by LlamaFactory, treat as sensitive exposure.
mitigations: Store account files in a separate directory.
Avoid placing secrets or account data in shared folders.
Delete temporary upload artifacts after use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, or use network egress, so it cannot contend with social-auto-upload over mutable resources. social-auto-upload has broad network egress but no filesystem write or git mutation, so there is no overlapping write surface to conflict on.
conditions: IF either profile gains filesystem write or git mutation in a shared directory, reassess conflict severity.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable OAuth scope, conflict may emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Run social-auto-upload with a dedicated account file.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
requires-engineering: add locking around any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: social-auto-upload can act on media and account data, so if it consumes LlamaFactory-generated text as authoritative instructions or metadata, mistakes can cascade into uploads or account actions. LlamaFactory has no built-in verification or action authority in the profile, so the risk is indirect but plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory output is used as upload captions, titles, or moderation decisions without review, cascading error exists.
IF social-auto-upload is configured to auto-publish based on generated text, blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing.
Use a validation step for captions and metadata.
Limit social-auto-upload to draft mode.
requires-engineering: add schema checks for LlamaFactory outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. LlamaFactory is open-source and touches no data classes, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media; the only clear compliance concern is operational handling of account-linked content, which is limited absent a stated regulated-data flow.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through social-auto-upload, compliance review is required.
IF account files contain jurisdiction-bound identifiers, reassess residency and retention controls.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of upload workflows.
Document retention for account files.
Separate personal and test accounts.
requires-engineering: add data-class tagging and residency controls.
